T: One last job. One hot meal.
D: A retired gunfighter turned pig farmer takes one last bounty in a Wyoming town run by a brutal sheriff.
P: Serve the mains when the riders finally get in out of the rain.
S: Pig farm crackling with apple sauce
Munny's struggling pig farm in Kansas

Pork rind scored, salted and dried overnight, roasted hot until blistered and crackling, broken into shards and served with warm spiced apple sauce. Score 600g pork rind every 1cm, rub with 1 tbsp salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Pat dry, lay skin up on a rack and roast at 240C for 30 minutes until puffed and blistered. Meanwhile, simmer 3 peeled, chopped green apples with 2 tbsp brown sugar, a pinch of cinnamon and 3 tbsp water for 10 minutes and mash. Break the crackling into shards and serve with the warm sauce.
the long ride north to Wyoming
Cornmeal, flour, buttermilk, egg and bacon fat mixed briefly, baked in a hot cast iron pan at 220C for 20 minutes.
Eggs boiled 10 minutes, peeled, pickled 3 days in hot vinegar with beetroot, sugar, mustard seed and peppercorns.
M: Rainy night beef and bean stew
sheltering from the rain on the trail
Beef chuck browned, onion, garlic and dried chilli, tomato and beans, braised at 160C for 3 hours until thick.
home on the farm with his children

Thick pork chops seared in cast iron, with apples and onions cooked golden in the same fat and a cider pan sauce, buttery mash and wilted greens. Season 4 thick pork chops and sear in a hot cast iron pan for 4 minutes a side, then rest. Add 20g butter, 2 sliced apples and a sliced onion and cook 8 minutes until golden. Pour in 150ml apple cider and 100ml chicken stock and reduce by half. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Wilt a bunch of silverbeet with garlic. Serve the chops with apples and sauce over the top.
W: Big Whiskey bread pudding, whiskey sauce
Greeley's saloon in Big Whiskey, Wyoming

Day-old bread baked in a cinnamon custard with raisins until puffed and golden, served warm under a buttery brown sugar whiskey sauce. Tear 400g day-old bread into a buttered dish with 80g raisins. Whisk 4 eggs, 600ml milk, 120g brown sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon, pour over and soak 20 minutes, then bake at 170C for 45 minutes until set and golden. Melt 80g butter with 100g brown sugar and 100ml cream, simmer 2 minutes and stir in 40ml whiskey. Pour over the warm pudding to serve.
K: the whiskey Munny swore off, until he doesn't

Strong boiled coffee sweetened with brown sugar and spiked with whiskey, poured into tin mugs and topped with a float of lightly whipped cream. Bring 1L water to the boil in a pot, stir in 60g coarse ground coffee and simmer 2 minutes. Take off the heat, splash in a little cold water to settle the grounds and rest 3 minutes. Lightly whip 150ml cream until just thick. Put 2 tsp brown sugar and 30ml whiskey in each of four mugs, pour in the coffee carefully and stir. Spoon the cream over the back of a spoon to float it on top.

s.note: the long ride north to Wyoming
s.how: Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp, chop and keep the fat in the pan. Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, an egg and 300ml buttermilk. Stir in the bacon, pour into the hot greased pan and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Serve with butter.

Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Heat 250ml white vinegar with the juice from a can of beetroot, 2 tbsp sugar, a teaspoon of mustard seeds and peppercorns. Pour over the eggs in a jar with the beetroot and pickle in the fridge for 3 days.

m.n: Rainy night beef and bean stew
m.note: sheltering from the rain on the trail
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add a sliced onion, crushed garlic and 2 crumbled dried chillies. Pour in a can of crushed tomatoes and water to cover. Braise at 160C for 3 hours, adding 2 cans of drained kidney beans for the last 30 minutes.
